title: Ethiopian Green Chilli Paste
community: All of Ethiopia — the green alternative to awaze
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Green Chilli Paste — fresh green jalapeños and serrano chillies blended with garlic, ginger, coriander, and a squeeze of lemon into a vibrant green condiment. The bright, fresh alternative to red awaze — used as a table condiment alongside grilled meats and fish.
longDesc: Green chilli paste is the fresh counterpart to the dried-chilli-based awaze — made from raw green jalapeños, it is brighter, more herbal, and has a different heat character than red awaze. Popular as a dipping sauce at Ethiopian restaurants.
steps: Combine all ingredients in a blender.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
chefTips: More jalapeños = more flavour (milder heat); more serranos = more heat.
The coriander adds fresh herbal brightness — do not omit.
commonMistakes: Not blending smooth enough — chunky is not right for this preparation.
cookingScience: Raw green chillies contain capsaicin in different chemical forms than dried red chillies — fresh chillies contain dihydrocapsaicin in higher proportions, which produces a slightly different heat sensation (broader, less pointy) than the capsaicin-dominant dried chilli heat.
healthBenefits: Vitamin C from raw chillies (much higher than dried).
culturalNote: Green chilli paste is the vibrant, fresh face of Ethiopian condiment culture — where awaze and berbere are the deep, complex, dried-chilli tradition, green paste represents the fresh-harvest season's brightness.
